description: Designing and delivering health services through digital technology: the digital health landscape and its evidence, mobile health applications, telemedicine models, tools for community health workers, remote monitoring and wearables, regulation and ethics, and the economics of scaling and sustaining digital health programmes. Taught through case-based simulations and prototypes built in the browser, from USSD and SMS services and offline-first community health worker apps to a teleconsultation flow between a rural clinic and a specialist.
modelledOn: WHO, Guideline: Recommendations on Digital Interventions for Health System Strengthening
WHO, Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health
WHO, Monitoring and Evaluating Digital Health Interventions: A Practical Guide
Wootton, Craig and Patterson, Introduction to Telemedicine
outcomes: Describe the digital health landscape using WHO classifications and appraise the evidence for digital interventions.
Design mobile health applications and services for low-bandwidth and basic-phone settings using SMS, USSD, voice and offline-first apps.
Compare synchronous, store-and-forward and remote monitoring telemedicine models and design a teleconsultation service with referral pathways.
Design and evaluate digital tools for community health workers that support decision making, reporting and supervision.
Analyse the regulatory, ethical and data protection requirements for a digital health product, including software as a medical device.
Plan the scale-up and sustainability of a digital health programme with costing, interoperability, governance and monitoring and evaluation.

units.title: Digital health landscape
topics: Digital health, eHealth, mHealth and telehealth defined; the WHO classification of digital health interventions
Health system challenges digital tools address: access, workforce shortages, information gaps, supply chains
The evidence base: what works, the pilot problem and the WHO digital health guideline
National digital health strategies and the WHO-ITU National eHealth Strategy Toolkit; Ghana's eHealth strategy
Stakeholders and business models: ministries, donors, start-ups, mobile network operators
The Principles for Digital Development

units.title: Mobile health applications
topics: Channels for basic phones: SMS, USSD and interactive voice response; local languages and low literacy
Smartphone apps: offline-first architecture, synchronisation and low data usage
Use cases: appointment reminders, adherence support, maternal messaging, health education, drug verification by SMS
Human-centred design with patients and health workers; designing for shared and low-end devices
Mobile money and health: insurance premium payments and mobile NHIS renewal
Building a USSD or SMS reminder service prototype

units.title: Telemedicine models
topics: Synchronous video and audio consultation, store-and-forward and remote monitoring compared
Specialties suited to telemedicine: teledermatology, teleradiology, telepathology, tele-ophthalmology, telepsychiatry
Hub-and-spoke teleconsultation between rural facilities and referral hospitals; national teleconsultation centres in Ghana
Technical requirements: bandwidth, latency, image quality, DICOM and secure messaging
Clinical governance: protocols, documentation, liability, licensing across borders
Simulated teleconsultation workflow from a CHPS compound to a specialist

units.title: Community health worker tools
topics: Community health workers and volunteers in African health systems; the CHPS model in Ghana
Decision support for community case management of malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea
Household registration, visit scheduling, referrals and follow-up; community-based surveillance
Platforms for CHW tools: Community Health Toolkit, CommCare, DHIS2 Android; offline data collection
Supervision, performance feedback and motivation through digital tools
Evaluating CHW tools: accuracy of classification, workload, data quality

units.title: Remote monitoring and wearables
topics: Remote patient monitoring for chronic disease: hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, pregnancy
Connected devices and wearables: blood pressure monitors, glucometers, pulse oximeters, activity trackers
Device data standards and integration: IEEE 11073, Bluetooth health profiles, FHIR observations
Signal quality, validation of consumer devices and alert thresholds
Point-of-care diagnostics with smartphones; AI-assisted screening

units.title: Regulation and ethics
topics: Software as a medical device: risk classification, IEC 62304, ISO 14971; the Ghana Food and Drugs Authority
Data protection: Ghana's Data Protection Act 843, the Malabo Convention, cross-border data transfer and cloud hosting
Informed consent, privacy and confidentiality in remote care; shared phones and family access
Equity and the digital divide: gender, rurality, literacy, disability, language
Ethics of AI in health: bias, accountability, explainability; WHO guidance on AI ethics
Security of mobile health systems: authentication, encryption, device loss

units.title: Scaling and sustaining digital health
topics: From pilot to national scale: pilotitis, government ownership and integration into the health system
Costing and economic evaluation: total cost of ownership, cost-effectiveness, financing models
Interoperability and digital public goods; avoiding vendor lock-in
Monitoring and evaluation frameworks for digital health; maturity models such as the Global Digital Health Monitor
Case studies: drone delivery of medical supplies, mobile maternal messaging, national telemedicine programmes in Africa

units.title: Project
topics: Identifying a health problem and the users affected through a needs assessment
Designing and prototyping a digital intervention with user feedback
Writing a regulatory, data protection and sustainability plan
Project: a working prototype with an evaluation plan and a pitch to a district health directorate

schedule.title: What digital health is and what the evidence says
schedule.exercise: Pick one digital health tool used in Ghana and write a half-page note placing it in the WHO classification and stating what evidence exists for it.

tasks.title: Classify eight real digital health interventions into the WHO categories of client, provider, system and data services and justify each placement
Match four health system gaps in a district to the digital tools that address them and score each match on feasibility in the case rubric
Appraise a pilot study of an SMS reminder programme, decide whether the evidence supports scaling, and explain the pilot problem in the debrief

schedule.title: Strategy, stakeholders and principles
schedule.exercise: Summarise Ghana's eHealth strategy in a table with its goals, owners and one risk for each, and add your own comment on gaps.

tasks.title: Map each strategy component of a national eHealth plan to a responsible ministry or agency and spot the two components with no owner
Choose a sustainable partnership model among a ministry, a donor, a start-up and a mobile network operator for a new app and defend the split of costs
Audit a proposed health app against the Principles for Digital Development and list which principles it breaks, with fixes ranked by impact

schedule.title: Mobile channels for basic phones and smartphones
schedule.exercise: Write the text of three appointment reminder messages in plain English with a local-language version of one, and justify the wording choices.

tasks.title: Design a USSD menu flow for checking a clinic appointment in three levels, then test every path on the phone emulator including a wrong input
Build an offline-first screen that stores patient visits locally and syncs them when a connection returns, then test it with the network off and on
Compare SMS, USSD and an app for four use cases in a rural district and recommend one channel per case within a data budget

schedule.title: Human-centred design and mobile money for health
schedule.exercise: Interview a classmate playing a community health nurse for 10 minutes and list three pain points that your design must address.

tasks.title: Adjust a given health app screen for a shared, low-end phone by simplifying text, enlarging controls and reducing images, then test it on a small screen
Walk through a mobile NHIS renewal case, choose payment and confirmation steps for a market trader, and score the result for access and risk
Prototype an SMS or USSD reminder service for antenatal visits with scheduling, language choice and opt-out, and test five user journeys

schedule.title: Telemedicine modes and specialties
schedule.exercise: Draw a diagram showing how a rural health worker, a district hospital and a specialist exchange information in a hub-and-spoke teleconsultation.

tasks.title: Choose between synchronous video, store-and-forward and remote monitoring for five patient cases and explain each choice in the scenario
Decide which of six specialties suit telemedicine at a rural clinic given bandwidth and staff constraints, and rank them for rollout
Run a hub-and-spoke teleconsultation from a rural facility to a referral hospital, deciding what to send and when to escalate, and score the outcome

schedule.title: Telemedicine technical and clinical governance
schedule.exercise: Write a short protocol for a teledermatology consultation, covering image quality, consent, documentation and follow-up.

tasks.title: Choose bandwidth, image resolution and secure messaging settings for a teleradiology link under a given data cap, and check the diagnostic quality
Resolve a liability and licensing question in a cross-border teleconsultation case by selecting the correct protocol and documentation steps
Build a simulated teleconsultation workflow from a CHPS compound to a specialist with referral, image upload and reply screens, and test a failed upload

schedule.title: Community health workers and decision support
schedule.exercise: Draw a one-page job aid for a community health worker classifying a child with fever and fast breathing, with clear referral signs.

tasks.title: Plan a day of household visits for a community health worker in a CHPS zone and prioritise visits using the risk information in the scenario
Build a decision-support form for malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea in a child and test it on 8 patient cases for correct classification
Create household registration, visit scheduling and referral screens that work offline and flag an overdue follow-up, then test a full month of visits

schedule.title: Platforms, supervision and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Design a short monthly feedback report for community health workers showing three indicators that motivate rather than punish.

tasks.title: Configure an offline data collection form for a household survey, enter 10 records without a network, and confirm they sync with no loss
Use dashboards of visit counts and data quality to decide which three health workers need supervision this month in a district case
Evaluate a community case-management tool from given test results for sensitivity, workload and data quality, and recommend whether to adopt it

schedule.title: Remote monitoring and connected devices
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph how a pregnant woman's blood pressure readings could be monitored from home and when an alert should be raised.

tasks.title: Choose a remote monitoring plan for a hypertensive patient in a case scenario, setting reading frequency, thresholds and escalation steps
Show a blood pressure reading from a connected device as a standard observation record on a phone screen and test it with five readings
Evaluate a consumer pulse oximeter against reference readings on darker skin tones and set alert thresholds that balance missed cases and false alarms

schedule.title: Regulation, privacy and consent
schedule.exercise: Write a plain-language consent paragraph for a remote care programme, covering what data is collected, who sees it and how to withdraw.

tasks.title: Classify three health apps by software as a medical device risk level and list the regulatory steps each would need
Review a clinic app's data flow against Ghana's Data Protection Act and decide which transfers to a foreign cloud need consent or safeguards
Handle a request from a family member for a patient's results on a shared phone, balancing confidentiality and care, and score your decision

schedule.title: Equity, AI ethics and security
schedule.exercise: Write a short note proposing three design changes that would make a health app usable by people with low literacy or disability.

tasks.title: Identify who is excluded by a proposed telemedicine rollout using given household data and propose two changes that widen access
Add login, local encryption and remote wipe for a lost device to a health app and test with a stolen-phone scenario
Audit a symptom-screening AI tool that performs worse on one group, decide whether to deploy and set safeguards in the scenario

schedule.title: Scale, cost and sustainability
schedule.exercise: Prepare a one-page case for a district health director on why a pilot should or should not be scaled, with costs and risks.

tasks.title: Plan the move of a successful pilot to government ownership by choosing integration, funding and training steps against a given timeline
Compare total cost of ownership and cost-effectiveness of two digital health options per patient served, and recommend one
Design a monitoring and evaluation framework for a national telemedicine programme and rate its maturity against a given model

schedule.title: Project: a digital health intervention
schedule.exercise: Present your intervention to a panel in five minutes, covering the problem, users, design, regulatory steps and how you will measure success.

tasks.title: Conduct a needs assessment from interview notes and data in a district case and write a problem statement naming the users affected
Prototype the main screens of your intervention and test them with five users, then record three changes you made from the feedback
Write the regulatory, data protection and sustainability plan for your intervention and defend it in a role-played district health directorate meeting
